term: Adult granulosa cell tumor of ovary
rationale: 'Adult granulosa cell tumor of ovary' names the ovarian entity specifically; the literature treats ovarian AGCT (FOXL2 p.Cys134Trp-driven, most common ovarian sex cord-stromal tumour) as distinct from the testicular counterpart in the code's ceiling, restricting this named term to the ovary (a proper subset of ovary+testis).

term: Granulosa cell tumor of ovary, NOS

source_name: Ricci et al., Histopathology 2025 (PMC12891927), WHO 5th ed male genital tumours

The term is therefore restricted to the adrenal gland, a proper subset of the ceiling (excludes mediastinal codes C381-C398).
source_name: Arch Pathol Lab Med (Tischler), summarizing WHO classification

rationale: As with pheochromocytoma NOS, WHO defines pheochromocytoma (including metastatic/malignant) as an intra-adrenal sympathetic paraganglioma; extra-adrenal/mediastinal tumors are paragangliomas. The named entity is restricted to the adrenal gland, a proper subset of the ceiling.
source_name: Arch Pathol Lab Med (Tischler), summarizing WHO classification

rationale: Pulmonary blastoma (pneumoblastoma) is defined by WHO Thoracic Tumours 5th ed as a rare subtype of lung cancer (biphasic tumor of the lung); it is a bronchopulmonary parenchymal tumor and is not a tracheal entity. It is thus restricted to lung/bronchus, a proper subset of the ceiling (excludes trachea C339 and respiratory NOS C390).
source_name: J Natl Cancer Center 2024 (citing WHO Thoracic Tumours 5th ed)

rationale: WHO Thoracic Tumours 5th ed defines pulmonary blastoma as a rare biphasic subtype of lung cancer arising in the lung; it is a bronchopulmonary tumor, not a tracheal one. Restricted to lung/bronchus, a proper subset of the ceiling (excludes trachea C339 and respiratory NOS C390).
source_name: J Natl Cancer Center 2024 (citing WHO Thoracic Tumours 5th ed)

rationale: Esthesioneuroblastoma arises from the specialized olfactory neuroepithelium of the upper nasal cavity, cribriform plate/ethmoid region, and olfactory nerve; ectopic occurrence in paranasal sinuses other than the ethmoid is vanishingly rare. It is therefore restricted to nasal cavity, ethmoid sinus, and olfactory nerve, a proper subset of the ceiling (excludes maxillary C310, frontal C312, sphenoid C313 sinuses and other cranial nerves).
source_name: Head Neck Pathol 2009 (Thompson, Olfactory Neuroblastoma)

rationale: Olfactory neuroblastoma (a synonym for esthesioneuroblastoma) arises from olfactory neuroepithelium in the upper nasal cavity, cribriform plate/ethmoid, and olfactory nerve; ectopic paranasal-sinus (non-ethmoid) tumors are vanishingly rare. Restricted to a proper subset of the ceiling (excludes maxillary, frontal, sphenoid sinuses and non-olfactory cranial nerves).
source_name: Head Neck Pathol 2009 (Thompson, Olfactory Neuroblastoma)

rationale: Fluid overload-associated LBCL presents as serous body-cavity effusions without detectable tumor masses, lymphadenopathy, or organ involvement, occurring in the pleural (majority), pericardial, and peritoneal cavities. Within this ceiling it is confined to pleura (C384) and pericardium (C380); peritoneum is not in the ceiling, and it does not involve the lung parenchyma, mediastinal tissue, bone marrow, spleen, or lymph nodes, so it is restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: SEER Hematopoietic Project (WHO 5th ed) - FO-LBCL

rationale: A synonym for fluid overload-associated LBCL, which presents as serous effusions confined to body cavities (pleural, pericardial, peritoneal) without tumor masses or organ involvement. Within this ceiling it is confined to pleura (C384) and pericardium (C380), a proper subset (excludes lung parenchyma, mediastinal tissue, bone marrow, spleen, lymph nodes).
source_name: SEER Hematopoietic Project (WHO 5th ed) - FO-LBCL

rationale: This is the WHO/ICC synonym for fluid overload-associated LBCL, an HHV8-negative effusion-based large B-cell lymphoma confined to serous body cavities (pleural, pericardial, peritoneal) without masses or organ involvement. Within this ceiling it is confined to pleura (C384) and pericardium (C380), a proper subset.
source_name: SEER Hematopoietic Project (WHO 5th ed) - FO-LBCL/effusion-based

term: Ductal carcinoma in situ, cribriform type
rationale: Ductal carcinoma in situ (intraductal carcinoma) is, by definition, a non-invasive carcinoma confined to the breast ducts/lobules; the 'ductal' cribriform-type in situ entity is a breast lesion, a proper subset of this code's ceiling which also spans skin and eye.
source_name: American Cancer Society — Understanding Your Pathology Report: Ductal Carcinoma In Situ (DCIS)

term: Ductal carcinoma in situ, solid type
rationale: Ductal carcinoma in situ, solid type is by definition a breast entity (malignant cells confined within breast ducts/lobules); it is anatomically restricted to the breast, a proper subset of this code's ceiling that also includes skin and thyroid.
source_name: American Cancer Society — Understanding Your Pathology Report: Ductal Carcinoma In Situ (DCIS)

rationale: Intraductal carcinoma is the direct synonym of ductal carcinoma in situ, a breast-duct-confined entity; the solid-type intraductal carcinoma is restricted to the breast, a proper subset of this code's ceiling that also includes skin and thyroid.
source_name: American Cancer Society — Understanding Your Pathology Report: Ductal Carcinoma In Situ (DCIS)

term: Mixed epithelioid and spindle cell uveal melanoma
rationale: A uveal melanoma is by definition an intraocular melanoma of the uveal tract (choroid, ciliary body, iris) of the eye; it does not arise on lip, skin or scrotum, so it is restricted to the intraocular (choroid C693 / ciliary body C694) subset of the ceiling.
source_name: NCI PDQ Intraocular (Uveal) Melanoma - uvea (iris, ciliary body, choroid) middle layer of the eye

rationale: By definition this lymphoma arises in the ocular adnexa (conjunctiva, orbit, lacrimal gland/drainage apparatus, and eyelid); the only ocular-adnexal skin site within its C44-based cutaneous ceiling is the skin of the eyelid (C441), a strict proper subset.
source_name: College of American Pathologists Ocular Adnexal Lymphoma protocol

rationale: Diverticular carcinoma arises within diverticula, which in the urinary tract occur as bladder diverticula and urethral diverticula; WHO 5th ed treats diverticular tumors as a separate site-specific entity. It does not arise in renal pelvis, ureter, or the female genital sites also in the code ceiling.
source_name: WHO 2022 bladder tumor classification news (diverticular tumors in specific section)
